all_found.desc: [BUG] The shared-store abandoned scan keeps a run only when canonical(work_dir) equals this worktree's toplevel exactly; fsm init --work-dir accepts any directory inside a worktree, so a subdirectory work_dir (or a removed worktree's) matches no worktree. The legacy fallback reads the CURRENT worktree's .metareview/runs (not the main checkout's single 0.13.x location), unscoped and without a warning. An abandoned run started with --work-dir <subdir> is never reported anywhere (reproduced: status blocked:false), letting the Stop gate pass; from a linked worktree its unmigrated runs are invisible and from main other branches' runs can falsely block.

[ADVISORY] Stale docs: driving-a-workflow.md and skills/fsm/SKILL.md:105 and docs/fsm/sdlc-loop-example.md:58 still put terminal/escalated rows in .metareview/runs.jsonl; ARCHITECTURE.md:123-127 still says runs live under the main worktree; commands/status.md:19, docs/README.codex.md:75, docs/README.claude.md:68 list .metareview/runs/; USAGE.md:259-260 is garbled; internal/repo/worktree.go:17-26, cmd/metareview/main.go:529-530 and session_test.go:135-137 comments describe the old store. Agents and readers look in the wrong place for runs and terminal rows.

[ADVISORY] TestFSMRootsAreDeclared now requires common-dir sites to declare `root: store (git's common directory)` and accepts `root: none`, but its doc comment, error message and ARCHITECTURE.md:194 still describe only root: store|work with store = main worktree; TestRunStoreReadersAreDeclared doc names only RunStoreRoot. Contributors hit an unexplained tripwire failure or misuse root: none.

rejected.desc: [BUG] MigrateLegacyRows runs on every fsm command (roots()), never records completion, strictly parses the main checkout's live per-worktree .metareview/runs.jsonl, and for each fsm-* row calls Exists and appendRow (each re-reading the common ledger under flock). O(legacy rows x ledger rows) on every fsm command forever (measured ~16.5s per `fsm state` with 2000 legacy rows), and one malformed line in that review ledger (lock-free AppendJSONL writers) makes every fsm command in every worktree fail with an ERR_RUNS_JSONL that names the wrong file.

findings.consequence: A regression in the primary record-lenses path passes CI; removing the fallback later breaks the suites wholesale.
findings.issue: writeFSMRun and the shell mkfsmrun helpers still forge runs under <root>/.metareview/runs, so every passing record-lenses --from-run end-to-end test exercises only the 0.13.x fallback; the common-dir read path has no integration test.

findings.consequence: The tripwires no longer guard the store they exist for; a new undeclared or mis-rooted common-dir reader passes.
findings.issue: TestFSMRootsAreDeclared (buildsRootedPath) and TestRunStoreReadersAreDeclared match only the .metareview spellings; neither sees the new "metareview", "runs" common-dir paths, and `root: store` now ambiguously means common dir or anchor.

findings.consequence: Agents and readers look in the wrong place for runs and terminal rows.

findings.consequence: They can drift (env scrubbing, path format) so sessions and the FSM store diverge.
findings.issue: Session bindings resolve the common dir themselves instead of via repo.StoreDir; there are now several common-dir resolvers.

findings.consequence: From such a subdirectory, status reports no abandoned runs, so the Stop gate can pass over an abandoned run.
findings.issue: here := canonical(root) uses the repo.Root result, not git's show-toplevel, while runs are attributed by Toplevel(work_dir); a status root in a monorepo subdirectory carrying its own docs/metareview or .metareview never equals a run's toplevel.

findings.consequence: Agents misread status output from a linked worktree.

findings.consequence: A run whose worktree was removed is reported from no checkout in that bare-repo + monorepo-subdir layout. Canonicalising main through Toplevel too would restore symmetry.
findings.issue: In a bare repository with linked worktrees, repo.RunStoreRoot falls back to RootOr(root), which stops at a subdirectory with its own docs/metareview, while here is now the worktree's toplevel, so here != main in every worktree.
